posts.title: The Court Answered, But Not the Question
posts.caption:
Central Valley public audit | administrative due process | Central Valley governance

📄 THE COURT ANSWERED, but it did not answer the question. The Tuolumne Court Executive Officer replied today: email is not the way to ask for a Presiding Judge review, put it in writing through the Clerk's Office, by mail or in person. The reply does not say the request reached Judge Krieg, does not name who receives it, and does not touch the November 5th review that is still unanswered in substance.

The next step is paper. The request goes out by mail, and the clock keeps running. Full breakdown in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio.

posts.title: A Year Ago, My Education Prospects Looked Bleak
posts.caption:
A YEAR AGO, MY EDUCATION PROSPECTS LOOKED BLEAK. TODAY MY PROFESSORS ARE TELLING ME MY WORK STANDS OUT. 📈

A year ago I did not know where my education would take me. I kept working anyway.

This week I read back my professor feedback. Dr. Tricia Kassab, on my EDDP 700 core values paper, wrote that my work "presents a highly authentic and personal exploration of the values that guide your leadership journey" and that my vision "reflects a strong commitment to equity, accountability, and community impact." She closed it with "Nice job!!"

Dr. Ashley McAdams, on my CSPU 640 analysis paper, wrote: "You clearly stated your perspective and provided detailed examples along with suggestions for improvement. Your paper is very well written and ready for submission."

That is two different professors, two different programs, saying the same thing. Clear perspective. Detailed examples. Well written. Authentic.

The push is consistent too, and I am taking it seriously. Dr. Kassab asked me to go deeper — less on organizational grievances, more on what those experiences shaped in my leadership philosophy and my future practice. That is fair. That is the work.

Here is how it connects to 209 Audit. The same discipline my professors are praising is the discipline I am building into the audit: separate what is documented from what I interpret from what is still unanswered. Write it plainly. Show the evidence. Say what you do not know yet. That is not neutral work and I do not pretend it is. It is careful work, and it is the work that makes the audit worth trusting.

My professional career is moving. My LinkedIn profile went from 817 viewers on Oct 10 to 1,048 viewers by Nov 13, with 14,062 post impressions. UC Merced is one of my strongest topics, and MCOE is the conversation I lead. A year ago I would not have expected that. Now I expect to have a lot of options soon, because the work is real and it is documented.

I am a doctoral student, an educator, and a public-records researcher. I am not done. I am just getting started.

— David

posts.caption:

📄 A THEORY WITH A TIMELINE. The district never gave a reason on paper, and the timing is the question. This is how you build a public record one document at a time: date every letter, quote the answer back word for word, and put a date on the next reply.

The record is the receipt. When there is no reason on paper, the paper trail is the argument, and the people kept in the dark are the ones who pay for it. Full story in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio.

posts.title: 978 Votes Separate Them. The Count Isn't Done
posts.caption:
Central Valley governance | Merced County spending | administrative accountability
🗳️ 978 VOTES. The count isn't done. Boyenga 33,611, Lopez 32,633, and the lead has moved on every update. About 650 ballots are still out, with 450 more waiting to be cured.

We asked the Registrar, on the record: how many ballots are left in each category, what is the cure rate, when is the next update, and what does the one percent manual tally show? Any voter can demand a recount in writing within five days of certification. That is the law.
